title: fix: array-literal args to pattern params, and flag-only defineProperty on host objects
author: claude
head: c74e8e2c73acdd20d8617b4ebc94890749506151
body:
Before: in JS-host mode, `function f([a, b = 9]) { return a + b; } f([1])` produced NaN (a standalone script threw `value is not iterable`). Separately, `Object.defineProperty(obj, "b", { enumerable: false })` on an object literal had no effect, so `Object.keys`, `values`, `entries` and `propertyIsEnumerable` still reported `b`. Both show up as failing files in PR #6044's harness sweep. Its CI requires every touched test file to pass in full, so these two bugs keep it from merging.

After: `f([1])` returns 10, and a flag-only `defineProperty` hides the field from those enumeration APIs.

How:
- **Param default ([#3643](https://js2wasm.loopdive.com/dashboard/issue.html?slug=3643-array-like-and-heterogeneous-vec-gaps)).** TypeScript types the argument `[1]` with the pattern's tuple type, so the host branch of `internal-call-argument.ts` built it as a tuple struct. The callee's destructuring only knows the vec representation, so it went looking for an iterator and failed. The literal is now built as a vec, which is what standalone mode already does. PR #6017 exposed this for nested function declarations, and bisection points at it. Top-level declarations were already affected.
- **enumerable:false ([#6472](https://js2wasm.loopdive.com/dashboard/issue.html?slug=6472-jshost-defineproperty-enumerable-false-not-honored-by-object-keys)).** `emitExternDefinePropertyNoValue` picked its compile-time struct branch from the TS type. It did so even when the literal had been compiled to a host plain object, and that branch evaluated the descriptor and then dropped it. Host objects now go to `__defineProperty_value`. An existing literal field also starts as a normal data property, so a later redefine is not rejected. The runtime enumeration code already reads that descriptor store.

`tests/issue-797-batch1.test.ts` gets the same one-line `setInstance` harness change that #6044 makes. The two edits are byte-identical, so the two PRs merge cleanly in either order.

## Verification

| file | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| issue-797-batch1 (setInstance harness) | 6/11 | 11/11 |
| new issue-3643-param-default | 0/4 | 4/4 |
| issue-3643-array-dstr-getiterator with #6044's harness | 13/14 | 14/14 |

Regression A/B, same HEAD, `JS2WASM_EVAL_ENGINE=interpreter`:
- **Destructuring / param / tuple / call-arg files** (105 files): 577 → 582 passing.
- **Array and equivalence files** (353 files): 2793 → 2794 passing.
- **Enumeration / descriptor / defineProperty files plus every `issue-3520-*` forgery-defence test** (101 files): only issue-797-batch1 changed.

No test went from passing to failing in any of these runs.

These gates are green locally: loc-budget, func-budget, coercion-sites, oracle-ratchet, dead-exports and host-import-policy. `src/runtime.ts` is untouched.

Still open:
- A flag-only define on an object that stays a real struct remains compile-time only, so `for-in` over it still lists the field. This is noted in the 797 issue file.
- `f([[1, 2], 3])` into `function f([[a, b], c])` still fails. It failed before this change too, and has a separate cause.
